html:
Syunik was a medieval Armenian kingdom in the mountains of southern Armenia, between Lake Sevan and the Araxes River. It existed from the 980s to 1170 and is shown here in 1100.

Syunik had long been ruled by its own princely family under the Bagratid kings of Armenia, and it became a kingdom in its own right in the late 10th century. Its great religious centre was Tatev, a monastery and school on a cliff above a gorge.

Syunik outlived the fall of Ani, but the Seljuks and their successors pressed on it. In 1170 they took its last fortress, Baghaberd, and the kingdom ended. Later the Orbelian princes ruled the region under Georgian and Mongol overlords. Its neighbours were Artsakh to the east and Tashir-Dzoraget to the north.
